dedupe_keys.name: liberia ministry of agriculture market price monitor monthly bulletins on imported rice and other food commodity prices across monitored markets

description: The Liberia Market Price Monitor is a short monthly bulletin from the Ministry of Agriculture on what staple foods cost in markets across the country. Each four-page issue reports month-on-month and year-on-year changes in the price of imported rice, the main staple, and other commodities by monitored market and county, with national averages and a commentary on causes such as inflation and currency depreciation. The April 2024 issue, for example, put a 25 kg bag of imported rice at 3,710 Liberian dollars nationally, about a fifth higher than a year before, with the sharpest rises in the south-east. The ministry's list holds five bulletins from September 2023 to April 2024 and three 2020 reports on market monitoring during the COVID-19 period, all free to download as PDFs. Caveats: the series is short and irregular, tables sit inside PDFs, no licence is stated, and the market sample is not described on the list page. Coverage is national. Simulation uses: regional price gradients for rice supply chain and port disruption studies in Liberia. Related records: the WFP global food prices database (data-wfp-global-food-prices) carries longer Liberian market price series.
